docs.title: Verbatim RAG
docs.text:
Chill, I Ground!

Provenance-first extractive RAG: select answer-relevant source passages and return them with citations instead of freely rewriting the evidence.

docs.title: Why Verbatim RAG?
docs.text:
Traditional RAG systems retrieve relevant documents and then allow an LLM to freely generate responses based on that context. This can lead to hallucinations where the model invents facts not present in the source material.

Verbatim RAG reduces unsupported generation by extracting source passages. Built-in verified paths return source text, but that contract does not guarantee source truth, retrieval recall, extraction relevance/completeness, or generated contextual framing. Use static templates for fixed deterministic framing.

docs.title: Two Packages
docs.text: Package Install Dependencies Use case verbatim-rag pip install verbatim-rag Full (torch, milvus, etc.) Complete RAG pipeline with indexing, search, and extraction verbatim-core pip install verbatim-core Lean (openai, pydantic, rapidfuzz, jinja2, typing_extensions) Reusable evidence transform for integration into existing systems

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Reduced generative surface -- Return evidence instead of freely paraphrasing it
  • Verbatim Extraction -- Built-in verified paths return text from supplied sources
  • Citation Tracking -- Responses include source citations and highlights
  • Multiple Extractors -- LLM-based, fine-tuned ModernBERT, or Zilliz semantic highlighting
  • Local static operation -- SPLADE + ModernBERT + static templates can run without generative LLM API calls
  • Template System -- Flexible response formatting with multiple strategies

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Document Processing -- Documents are processed using docling and chunked with chonkie
  2. Document Indexing -- Indexed using vector embeddings (dense and/or sparse)
  3. Query Processing -- Relevant documents are retrieved
  4. Span Extraction -- Key passages are extracted verbatim
  5. Response Generation -- Templates structure the answer with citations

docs.title: Migrating to 0.3.0
docs.text:
0.3.0 adds a stateless core: extractors return spans with their chunk ids and offsets, and a Transformer turns a question and chunks into a cited answer. VerbatimRAG is built on a Transformer you pass in. Models and LLM clients are passed into constructors, and the settings of a request are arguments of the call.

The old entry points keep working through the 0.3.x and 0.4.x releases. Each one warns with VerbatimDeprecationWarning, a DeprecationWarning, whose message names its replacement:

VerbatimTransform is deprecated since 0.3.0 and will be removed in 0.5.0. Use Transformer.

They are removed in 0.5.0.

docs.title: Finding the old calls
docs.text:
Python hides DeprecationWarnings outside __main__. Turn the library's warnings into errors in your tests to find every old call:

# pyproject.toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
filterwarnings = ["error::verbatim_core.VerbatimDeprecationWarning"]

Or show them while running a script: python -W always::DeprecationWarning your_script.py. Importing either package never warns; using an old name does, including importing a name from a moved module such as verbatim_rag.transform.

docs.title: Answering from chunks
docs.text:
VerbatimTransform took context dicts and returned a QueryResponse. Build a Transformer from an extractor and templates instead, pass it chunks, and turn its Answer into a QueryResponse when you need one:

# Before
from verbatim_core import VerbatimTransform

vt = VerbatimTransform(template_mode="contextual", max_display_spans=5)
response = vt.transform(question, context)

# After
from verbatim_core import Chunk, TransformConfig, Transformer
from verbatim_core.extractors import LLMSpanExtractor
from verbatim_core.llm_client import LLMClient
from verbatim_core.response_builder import ResponseBuilder
from verbatim_core.templates import TemplateManager

client = LLMClient("gpt-4o-mini")
transformer = Transformer(
    LLMSpanExtractor(client),
    TemplateManager(llm_client=client, default_mode="contextual"),
    config=TransformConfig(max_display_spans=5),
)

chunks = [
    Chunk(id=f"ctx_{i}", text=item["content"], metadata={"title": item.get("title", "")})
    for i, item in enumerate(context)
]
answer = transformer.transform(question, chunks)
response = ResponseBuilder().build_from_answer(question, answer, chunks)

A chunk's id is yours to choose, unique within a call; the answer's citations point at it with offsets into its text.

Old New VerbatimTransform(...), transform, transform_async Transformer(extractor, templates, config=TransformConfig(...)), transform, atransform, then ResponseBuilder().build_from_answer verbatim_query(provider, question, k) context = provider.retrieve(question, k=k), chunks from the context items as above, Transformer.transform, then ResponseBuilder().build_from_answer verbatim_query_async(provider, question, k) context = await provider.retrieve_async(question, k=k), chunks from the context items as above, Transformer.atransform, then ResponseBuilder().build_from_answer verbatim_rag.transform.VerbatimTransform, verbatim_query, verbatim_query_async the same names from verbatim_core, then the rows above verbatim_rag.transform.SearchResult verbatim_rag.vector_stores.SearchResult

docs.title: Extractors
docs.text:
extract takes chunks and returns an Extraction: spans with their chunk ids, offsets and scores, the usage of the call and its warnings. extract_spans returned span texts keyed by chunk text.

# Before
spans_by_text = extractor.extract_spans(question, search_results)

# After
extraction = extractor.extract(question, chunks)
for span in extraction.spans:
    print(span.chunk_id, span.start, span.end, span.text)
Old New extractor.extract_spans(question, results) extractor.extract(question, chunks) extractor.extract_spans_async(question, results) await extractor.aextract(question, chunks) A SpanExtractor subclass that implements only extract_spans Implement extract(self, question, chunks, *, config=None), returning an Extraction. Until then, extract locates the span texts in their chunks and warns. A subclass of LLMSpanExtractor or another extractor that overrides extract_spans, for example to filter the spans Override extract instead, and filter the Extraction's spans. Until then, extract and aextract call your extract_spans and warn. LLMSpanExtractor(), LLMSpanExtractor(model="gpt-4o") LLMSpanExtractor(LLMClient("gpt-4o")) LLMSpanExtractor(client, model=...) The model of the client: LLMClient(model) LLMSpanExtractor(client, extraction_mode=..., batch_size=..., span_match_mode=..., fuzzy_threshold=..., extraction_prompt=..., system_prompt=...) LLMSpanExtractor(client, config=LLMExtractConfig(...)) with the same names LLMSpanExtractor(..., max_display_spans=...), ModelSpanExtractor(..., max_display_spans=...) Transformer(..., config=TransformConfig(max_display_spans=...)) ModelSpanExtractor(), ModelSpanExtractor("org/model"), ModelSpanExtractor(model_path=..., device=...) ModelSpanExtractor.from_pretrained("org/model", device=...) ModelSpanExtractor(..., threshold=..., min_span_chars=..., merge_gap_chars=..., max_length=..., doc_stride=...) config=ModelExtractConfig(...) with the same names ModelSpanExtractor(..., extraction_mode=...) Nothing in its place: it had no effect SemanticHighlightExtractor(), SemanticHighlightExtractor("org/model"), SemanticHighlightExtractor(model_name=..., device=..., max_tokens=...) SemanticHighlightExtractor.from_pretrained("org/model", device=..., max_tokens=...) SemanticHighlightExtractor(..., threshold=..., output_mode=..., language=..., min_span_tokens=..., merge_gap=...) config=SemanticHighlightConfig(...) with the same names

from_pretrained is the one place a model name becomes a loaded model, so you decide when the download happens. A loaded model can also be passed in: ModelSpanExtractor(model).

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
The settings of a TemplateManager are its config, the default of every Transformer built with it. Pass other settings to the Transformer or to one call instead of changing the templates:

# Before
templates.set_mode("random")
templates.set_citation_mode("hidden")

# After: for every call of this transformer
transformer = Transformer(
    extractor, templates, config=TransformConfig(template_mode="random", citation_mode="hidden")
)
# or for one call
answer = transformer.transform(question, chunks, config=TransformConfig(template_mode="random"))
Old New TemplateManager.set_mode(mode), assigning TemplateManager.current_mode TransformConfig(template_mode=mode); for structured mode, TemplateManager.use_structured_mode() TemplateManager.set_citation_mode(mode), assigning TemplateManager.citation_mode TransformConfig(citation_mode=mode) TemplateManager.set_citation_format(format) TransformConfig(citation_format=format) Contextual template mode without an LLM client, which used the static template TemplateManager(llm_client=client) TemplateManager.set_rag_system, StructuredTemplate.set_rag_system, StructuredTemplate.fill_async VerbatimRAG.query_async, which answers structured questions itself QuestionSpecificTemplate(model_name=..., device=...), question-specific templates without an embedder QuestionSpecificTemplate.from_pretrained(model_name, device, templates=...), or embedder= a loaded model, also in TemplateManager.use_question_specific_mode(templates, embedder=...)

docs.title: VerbatimRAG
docs.text:
VerbatimRAG takes the Transformer that writes its answers, and k is an argument of each query:

# Before
rag = VerbatimRAG(index, model="gpt-4o-mini", k=5, template_mode="contextual", max_display_spans=5)
response = rag.query(question)

# After
client = LLMClient("gpt-4o-mini")
transformer = Transformer(
    LLMSpanExtractor(client),
    TemplateManager(llm_client=client, default_mode="contextual"),
    config=TransformConfig(max_display_spans=5),
)
rag = VerbatimRAG(index, transformer=transformer, llm_client=client)
response = rag.query(question, k=5)

The llm_client of VerbatimRAG serves structured template mode, which answers without the Transformer. Nothing is set on VerbatimRAG by a call, so one instance can serve concurrent queries.

Old New VerbatimRAG(index), and the arguments model, template_manager, extractor, max_display_spans, template_mode and extraction_mode VerbatimRAG(index, transformer=Transformer(extractor, templates, config=...), llm_client=client) VerbatimRAG(index, k=...) rag.query(question, k=...), query_async and query_stream likewise, and VerbatimDOC(rag, k=...) Assigning rag.extractor or rag.template_manager A VerbatimRAG with a Transformer of that extractor and those templates Assigning rag.max_display_spans Transformer(..., config=TransformConfig(max_display_spans=...)) StreamingRAG(rag).stream_query(question, num_docs, ...), stream_query_sync rag.query_stream(question, k=..., ...) verbatim_rag.document.Chunk verbatim_rag.document.DocumentChunk

query_stream yields typed events instead of dicts, and raises instead of sending an error event:

# Before
async for event in StreamingRAG(rag).stream_query(question, num_docs=5):
    if event["type"] == "documents":
        show_sources(event["data"])
    elif event["type"] == "answer":
        show_answer(event["data"])

# After
async for event in rag.query_stream(question, k=5):
    if event.type == "documents":
        show_sources(event.chunks)
    elif event.type == "spans":
        highlight(event.spans)
    else:
        show_answer(event.response)

The last event carries the same QueryResponse that query returns for the same input.

docs.title: What changes without a warning
docs.text:
Some behaviour changes in 0.3.0 for the old entry points too. The changelog has the details:

  • A failed LLM call during extraction raises an UpstreamError or a ConfigurationError, instead of answering from the remaining chunks (ADR 0006).
  • One span gives one highlight and one citation, where the span is, instead of one at every occurrence of its text (ADR 0001).
  • Random template mode gives the same question the same template.
  • A context item of the wrong shape raises InvalidInputError, a ValueError, instead of TypeError: except TypeError no longer catches it.
  • A QueryResponse lists in warnings how its answer is degraded but still correct, such as quotes that couldn't be located.
  • The steps of a call log at DEBUG, and customer text is logged only on the verbatim_core.content logger. See Errors, warnings and logs.

docs.title: Stateless core: open questions for VerbatimRAG
docs.text:
This file collects the decisions VerbatimRAG needs before the stateless-core work ("One interface per capability: stateless core, stores passed in") can be implemented in this repository. Answers that are decided here become ADRs; terms that get sharpened go into GLOSSARY.md.

The questions are split in three groups:

  • Decided here: only VerbatimRAG is affected, or VerbatimRAG can decide its part on its own.
  • Decided elsewhere: cross-library questions. VerbatimRAG waits for the answer and lists what it needs from it.
  • Not relevant: questions from the design doc that don't touch this repository.

Each question has a recommended answer. A recommendation is not a decision until the Decision field is filled in.

docs.title: Decided here
docs.text:
❓ Q1 - Score for LLM span extraction (design doc, open question 3)

LLMSpanExtractor produces no probability, but Span.score is a required float and min_score filters on it. What does score hold for spans the LLM extracted?

➡️ 1.0, documented as "extracted without a score", so score is always a number and a min_score filter keeps these spans. This must match what LettuceDetect decides for the LLM judge without reasoning, so confirm with the LettuceDetect side before writing the ADR.

Decision: 1.0, documented as "extracted without a score". The fuzzy matcher's match quality does not go into score: it says how faithfully a quote was located, not how relevant it is. VerbatimRAG has no min_score; nothing on this side filters or sorts by score. The ADR waits until LettuceDetect picks the same value for the judge without reasoning. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q2 - Default LLM client after the deprecation window (design doc, open question 4)

During the window, VerbatimRAG(index), LLMSpanExtractor() and TemplateManager() without a client build LLMClient(model) as today and warn. After the window, is the client required?

➡️ Required wherever an LLM is actually called, and nowhere else. A VerbatimRAG with a ModelSpanExtractor and static templates calls no LLM and should need no client at all. The READMEs show the explicit form from 0.3.0 on.

Decision: Correction to the question: TemplateManager never builds a client. Without one, contextual mode silently falls back to static with a print (templates/manager.py:65). - LLMSpanExtractor(llm_client): the client is required after the window. During the window, omitting it builds LLMClient(model) and warns. - TemplateManager: the client stays optional. During the window, contextual mode without a client still falls back to static but warns. After the window it raises a typed error, at the call and at Transformer construction when the default config already needs a client. - VerbatimRAG: after the window it takes no model, and llm_client only for structured mode (Q8). Structured mode without a client raises. - The READMEs show the explicit form from 0.3.0 on. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q3 - Span text for fuzzy matches

The design doc requires that a span's text always equals the slice at its offsets. With fuzzy matching (verbatim_core/extractors.py:838), the quote the LLM returned and the matched slice of the chunk can differ. Which one is Span.text, and what happens to a quote that matches nothing above the threshold?

➡️ Span.text is the slice of the chunk, never the LLM's quote. A quote without a match is dropped and reported in Extraction.warnings, not silently discarded, in line with "Typed errors, and no fallbacks that hide a failure".

Decision: Span.text is the slice of the chunk, which both match modes already return today; the matchers now return the offsets too. A quote without a match is dropped and reported in Extraction.warnings. "Quote" (the string the LLM returns) and "span" (its located slice) are defined in GLOSSARY.md. (2026-11-02)

Revised: the offsets work no longer waits for PR #79 (#34). Fixing #34 well is a larger problem than it looks, so it is done separately. The locator uses today's fuzzy matcher, changed only to return offsets with the text and kept behind one function, which the fix for #34 replaces. The fuzzy-mode fixtures record today's matcher, and that fix updates them as an intended change. (2026-11-03)

❓ Q4 - Which occurrence of a repeated quote

When a quote occurs more than once in a chunk, the extractor picks one occurrence (design doc, verbatim.extract). Model extractors get offsets from the model, so this only concerns the LLM extractor and subclasses written against the old interface. Which occurrence is picked?

➡️ The first exact occurrence; if there is none, the best fuzzy match. Documented in the ADR and in the changelog entry that already covers "highlights the chosen occurrence instead of every occurrence".

Decision: The first exact occurrence, else the best fuzzy match, the earliest on a tie. Identical (start, end) spans collapse into one. The response builder keeps today's first-wins rule for overlapping highlights. The changelog entry also says that repeated text now gets one citation instead of one per occurrence, since today every highlighted occurrence gets its own citation number. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q5 - Where Chunk.id comes from

ExtractedSpan.chunk_id points at a Chunk.id. SearchResult.to_chunk() has to fill it, and the deprecated extract_spans adapter builds chunks from positions (_chunk_from_result(i, result)). Is a chunk id meant to be stable beyond a single call, for example in citations returned by the API?

➡️ Yes. SearchResult.to_chunk() uses the id the index stores for the chunk, stable across queries. Positional ids are only used inside the deprecated adapters, where the id never leaves the call. Chunks sent with a request to verbatim.transform keep the ids the caller gave them.

Decision: SearchResult.to_chunk() uses SearchResult.id, the vector row id (ProcessedChunk.id, a random UUID). It is stable while the document stays indexed but not across re-indexing, and the documentation says so. A deterministic "{document_id}:{chunk_number}" was rejected: after a chunking change it would silently point at different text. Positional ids are used only inside the deprecated adapters; ids sent to verbatim.transform are kept as given. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q6 - Streaming events and today's API

Transformer.stream and astream yield a spans event and an answer event. VerbatimRAG.query_stream sends a documents event first. StreamingRAG (verbatim_rag/streaming.py) and the route at api/app.py:350 emit today's event dicts. Does query_stream yield typed TransformEvent objects or today's dicts, and what exactly is in each event?

➡️ query_stream yields typed events. The deprecated StreamingRAG adapter converts them to today's dicts, and the existing streaming route keeps its current shape until a new route replaces it. Define the fields of the documents, spans and answer events in the ADR.

Decision: query_stream yields typed events: documents (the chunks), spans (the ExtractedSpans), and a final event carrying the same QueryResponse that query returns, so the two are testably equal. Errors raise typed exceptions instead of arriving as events. progress is not a typed event; the StreamingRAG adapter rebuilds it from timing. The existing route keeps today's five event types (documents, progress, highlights, answer, error). (2026-11-02)

❓ Q7 - The name Chunk is already taken

verbatim_rag/document.py:157 defines Chunk, the ingestion record (document_id, content, start_index, end_index, chunk_number, chunk_type, processed_chunks), which users pass in to index pre-chunked documents. The shared Chunk is the core's input. The default chunker never fills start_index and end_index, and they aren't stored.

➡️ "Chunk" means the shared core type. The ingestion dataclass becomes DocumentChunk, with verbatim_rag.document.Chunk as a deprecated alias. Indexed chunks have source_start and source_end set to None until the index stores them.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q8 - Structured template mode

The design doc doesn't cover template_mode="structured". VerbatimRAG.query branches on it (verbatim_rag/core.py:250, :344) and calls self.llm_client.extract_structured(...) directly, bypassing SpanExtractor. TemplateManager and StructuredTemplate hold a back-reference to the RAG object (set_rag_system), and their fill_async calls rag_system.query_async. Issue #74 redesigns structured answers.

➡️ Structured mode stays out of the core for this rollout, as a documented exception inside VerbatimRAG. Transformer raises if asked for it. fill_async and set_rag_system are deprecated. #74 brings structured answers into the core as their own capability.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q9 - Template settings changed between calls

TemplateManager has setters that change it between calls: set_mode, set_citation_mode, set_citation_format, use_structured_mode (templates/manager.py:69, :377, :456, :468). A Transformer shared across requests would race on them.

➡️ TransformConfig carries template_mode, citation_mode and citation_format. The TemplateManager constructor arguments become the default config, the setters become deprecated adapters that replace it, and nothing in the core reads current_mode.

Decision: Accepted as recommended, except use_structured_mode (see Q12). TemplateManager.save and load stay: "the core writes nothing to disk" applies to capability calls, and these are explicit I/O the caller asks for at setup (Q14). (2026-11-02)

❓ Q10 - Random and question-specific templates

RandomTemplate.generate uses random.choice per call (templates/random.py:101), which fails "same input, same result". QuestionSpecificTemplate loads a SentenceTransformer by name inside a call (templates/question_specific.py:84) and caches embeddings on self.

➡️ Random mode picks its template from a stable hash of the question, with an optional seed in TransformConfig. QuestionSpecificTemplate takes a loaded embedder, with from_pretrained(model_name) as the one place a name becomes a model, and embeds its examples at construction.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q11 - A failed LLM call silently returns no spans

In batch mode a failed call falls back to individual calls (verbatim_core/extractors.py:616). If that fails too, or in individual mode, the chunk gets no spans with only a logger.error (:740, :771). The caller can't tell "nothing relevant" from "never examined".

➡️ A failed LLM call raises a typed error and extract fails as a whole. Retries belong in the LLM-call layer. The batch-to-individual fallback stays only in the deprecated path.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q12 - Q8 and Q9 conflict on use_structured_mode

Q9 deprecates every TemplateManager setter, including use_structured_mode, but Q8 keeps structured mode with no replacement until #74. A deprecation warning has to name a replacement.

➡️ use_structured_mode and the structured template's setup are left out of Q9's deprecation. VerbatimRAG keeps detecting structured mode from the template manager's mode, as today. The whole structured API is deprecated in one step when #74 provides the replacement. fill_async is deprecated now, in favour of VerbatimRAG.query_async.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q13 - Duplicate chunks in one call

A verbatim.transform request can send two chunks with the same id, which makes ExtractedSpan.chunk_id ambiguous. Retrieval can return two rows with identical text, the processed versions of one document chunk (verbatim_rag/index.py:392); today extract_spans merges them because it keys its result by text.

➡️ Duplicate ids in one call raise a typed input error. Chunks with the same text but different ids are extracted independently, with no merging by text.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q14 - TemplateManager.save and load

TemplateManager.save(filepath) and load(filepath) read and write JSON (templates/manager.py:195), and TemplateManager is passed into the core Transformer.

➡️ They stay: explicit I/O the caller asks for at setup, never a side effect of transform.

Decision: Accepted as recommended, and recorded with Q9. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q15 - Which decisions get an ADR

➡️ ADRs for Q1 (after LettuceDetect agrees), Q4, Q5, Q6, Q8 with Q12, Q10 and Q11, in docs/adr/ numbered from 0001. Q3, Q7 and Q9 need none: GLOSSARY.md and the design doc explain them.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. Written: docs/adr/0001 (Q4) to 0006 (Q11). The Q1 ADR waits for LettuceDetect. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q16 - Frontend stream errors

The frontend drops error events (frontend/src/contexts/ApiContext.js:165), so a failed streamed query stops loading without a message. This is a bug in today's code, independent of the stateless-core work.

➡️ File it once these questions are settled, as Bug: streamed query errors never reach the user, labelled bug and needs-triage.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. Filed as #85. (2026-11-02)

❓ Q17 - query and query_stream count display citations differently

The response builder marks citation n as display while n ≤ display_span_count. VerbatimRAG.query and query_async pass len(all_relevant_spans), the number of chunks (verbatim_rag/core.py:271, :369). StreamingRAG and both VerbatimTransform copies pass len(display_spans), the number of spans shown in the answer. Q6 requires the two to return equal responses.

➡️ The number of spans shown is right, and query's count is a bug. File it next to Q16 as Bug: VerbatimRAG.query marks citations as display by chunk count, and fix it before the rollout so the regression fixtures record the fixed behaviour.

Decision: Accepted as recommended. Filed as #86. (2026-11-02)

docs.title: One interface per capability: stateless core, stores passed in
docs.text:
This document expands the idea-box entry of the same name. It defines the stateless interface for each capability verbatim-rag exposes, the types those interfaces share, the store interfaces the stateful classes are built on, and how today's public API keeps working with a deprecation warning until it is removed. Everything here is a proposal until the entry becomes an issue. The questions the team has to decide are collected at the end.

The capabilities are verbatim.extract and verbatim.transform with its streaming variant.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
The library has two layers.

The stateless core has one interface per capability. A call takes a typed request and returns a typed result, and the result depends only on the input, the model version and the config. Code in the core:

  • writes nothing to disk and keeps nothing between calls
  • has no global state and reads no environment variables
  • never builds a model or an LLM client from a name inside a constructor. The loaded model or the client is passed in
  • takes and returns the shared types Chunk, Span and Usage.

The stateful classes (VerbatimRAG, VerbatimIndex) keep today's convenience for open-source users. They are built from the core and from stores passed to them. Their own code retrieves, stores and calls the core, and nothing else.

Today's public API stays. Every class, function, method and argument that the core replaces becomes an adapter over the core, warns when it is used, and is removed after a deprecation window. Each step has one implementation, so the old and the new API can't drift apart.

docs.title: Shared types
docs.text:
These types are the vocabulary of every interface below. They live in verbatim_core.

class Chunk(BaseModel):
    """A piece of source text."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    id: str
    text: str
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {}
    source_start: int | None = None  # position of the chunk in its source document
    source_end: int | None = None


class Span(BaseModel):
    """A part of a text, as "One span format across the libraries" defines it."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    start: int  # Unicode code points, inclusive
    end: int  # exclusive
    text: str  # always equal to the slice it points into
    score: float


class Usage(BaseModel):
    """What one model or service did during a call."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    model_id: str | None  # None for work without a model
    model_version: str | None
    units: dict[str, int]  # for example {"chunks": 12, "input_tokens": 3410}
  • A span's offsets are relative to the chunk it comes from. Fields specific to extraction go into a subclass: ExtractedSpan adds chunk_id.
  • Every result carries usage: list[Usage], one entry per model or service that took part. A transform has one entry for the extractor model and one for the LLM that wrote the template. The library reports every unit it can count (chunks, characters, tokens, LLM calls).
  • model_version identifies the weights exactly. from_pretrained records the resolved Hugging Face commit, not the repository id. For weights mounted from a local path (see "Mount local model weights and configure their paths in pydantic-settings configs") the caller passes model_version, because a path doesn't say which weights it holds. For a third-party LLM it is the model name the provider returned.
  • Every result also carries warnings, and batch results carry failures, as "Typed errors, and no fallbacks that hide a failure" defines.
  • The types are pydantic models because they cross the API boundary unchanged.

docs.title: Results are objects, not lists
docs.text:
The idea-box entry writes extract(question, chunks) -> list[Span]. A list has no place for usage and warnings, so each capability returns a result object:

Capability Result Fields verbatim.extract Extraction spans: list[ExtractedSpan], usage, warnings verbatim.transform Answer text, citations, spans: list[ExtractedSpan], usage, warnings

docs.title: The method set
docs.text:
Every stateless interface has the same methods. A capability adds streaming methods only where it needs them.

Capability Interface Sync Async Streaming verbatim.extract SpanExtractor extract aextract – verbatim.transform Transformer transform atransform stream, astream
  • Long calls take an on_progress callback that reports their progress. This is the callback that open question 1 of the logging convention recommends.
  • The methods follow "Write each step once, with thin sync and async wrappers". The logic lives in functions without I/O, and the sync and async methods only make the calls. Local encoder inference runs in a worker thread behind the async method.
  • The constructor takes what the interface depends on: a loaded model, an LLM client and a default config. Everything a caller may choose per request is a call argument, and a config argument replaces the default config for one call. Nothing is set on the object between calls.

docs.title: verbatim.extract
docs.text:
class SpanExtractor(ABC):
    def extract(
        self, question: str, chunks: Sequence[Chunk], *, config: ExtractConfig | None = None
    ) -> Extraction: ...

    async def aextract(
        self, question: str, chunks: Sequence[Chunk], *, config: ExtractConfig | None = None
    ) -> Extraction: ...

SpanExtractor stays the base class. It gains the two methods, and extract_spans becomes the deprecated adapter (see "Subclasses written against the old interface").

Extractor Constructor Where the offsets come from score ModelSpanExtractor, highlighter models ModelSpanExtractor(model, config=...) and ModelSpanExtractor.from_pretrained(model_id, device=None) .process() returns character spans. Today the extractor keeps only their text (verbatim_core/extractors.py:222) the model's span probability ModelSpanExtractor, v1 sentence model the same the sentence boundaries from the splitter the sentence probability SemanticHighlightExtractor from_pretrained as above. Today the constructor loads the model (:336) the token regions it computes already the region probability LLMSpanExtractor LLMSpanExtractor(llm_client, config=...), with the client required the extractor locates each quote in the chunk it came from. The fuzzy matcher already works with offsets and returns only the text (:838) open question 2

ExtractConfig holds today's constructor settings: the threshold, min_span_chars, merge_gap_chars, max_length and doc_stride for the model, and the extraction mode, batch size, match mode and prompts for the LLM.

When a quote occurs more than once in a chunk, the extractor picks one occurrence. Today the response builder searches for the span text afterwards and highlights every occurrence (verbatim_core/response_builder.py:122).

docs.title: verbatim.transform
docs.text:
class Transformer:
    def __init__(
        self,
        extractor: SpanExtractor,
        templates: TemplateManager,
        *,
        config: TransformConfig | None = None,
    ) -> None: ...

    def transform(
        self, question: str, chunks: Sequence[Chunk], *, config: TransformConfig | None = None
    ) -> Answer: ...

    async def atransform(...) -> Answer: ...

    def stream(...) -> Iterator[TransformEvent]: ...

    async def astream(...) -> AsyncIterator[TransformEvent]: ...
  • transform is today's VerbatimTransform.transform without the conversion of dicts into search results. The response builder builds citations and highlights from the span offsets.
  • TransformConfig holds the number of displayed spans and the template mode.
  • TemplateManager gets its LLM client passed in. The static template mode needs none.
  • stream and astream yield a spans event after extraction and an answer event at the end. They need no index, so verbatim.transform-stream works on chunks sent with the request.
  • The answer argument, which VerbatimTransform.transform accepts and ignores today, is not carried over.

docs.title: Stores
docs.text:
Stored state sits behind typing.Protocol interfaces that the caller passes into the stateful classes. The library ships local implementations, and callers can pass their own. No method takes an owner id: a caller passes in a store already limited to the data it may read, so library code can't read other data by mistake.

The one store holds vectors and documents. Its protocol is VectorStore, defined in "Make the vector store easy to swap", its implementations are Milvus Lite and Milvus Cloud, as today, and VerbatimIndex uses it.

docs.title: Models and clients are passed in
docs.text:
• A class that runs a model takes the loaded model in its constructor. A from_pretrained(model_id, ...) classmethod is the one place where a name becomes a model, so the caller decides when the download and the load happen: at startup in a server, in the first cell of a notebook.
  • from_pretrained accepts a local path, which is how a container loads weights mounted into it.
  • A class that calls an LLM takes the client. The client comes from "One LLM-call layer in each library". Until that layer exists, it is LLMClient, the client verbatim-rag takes today.
  • A model served remotely is passed in as a client. An encoder served remotely becomes one more implementation of the same interface.

docs.title: VerbatimRAG and VerbatimIndex
docs.text:
transformer = Transformer(
    extractor=ModelSpanExtractor.from_pretrained("KRLabsOrg/verbatim-rag-modern-bert-v2"),
    templates=TemplateManager(llm_client=LLMClient("gpt-4o-mini")),
)
rag = VerbatimRAG(index, transformer=transformer)
response = rag.query("What does the warranty cover?", k=5)
  • query retrieves from the index, converts the search results to Chunk, calls transformer.transform and builds the QueryResponse it returns today. query_async does the same with atransform.
  • query_stream(question, k=...) replaces StreamingRAG. It sends the documents event, then the events of transformer.astream. k is an argument. Today StreamingRAG sets rag.k on the shared object for one request (verbatim_rag/streaming.py:53).
  • Intent detection and reranking stay in VerbatimRAG. They are pipeline stages around the core.
  • VerbatimIndex already takes its vector store and embedding providers. Its query keeps returning SearchResult (verbatim_rag/index.py:552), and SearchResult.to_chunk() converts a result before it reaches the core. The store interface belongs to "Make the vector store easy to swap".

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text: A stateful class may still create a local store when none is passed, because keeping state locally is what the class is for. It never builds a model or an LLM client from a name. When the caller passes none, the class builds today's default for the length of the deprecation window and warns, so the quickstarts in the READMEs keep running. Open question 3 asks what happens after the window.

docs.title: Deprecating today's API
docs.text: Every public name that the core replaces stays available, warns when it is used, and is removed after the deprecation window (open question 1).

docs.title: Adapters only
docs.text:
An old entry point converts its arguments to the new types, calls the core and converts the result back to today's shape. It keeps no logic of its own:

class SpanExtractor(ABC):
    @deprecated("SpanExtractor.extract_spans", since="0.3.0", removed_in="0.5.0", use="extract()")
    def extract_spans(self, question: str, search_results: list[Any]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        chunks = [_chunk_from_result(i, result) for i, result in enumerate(search_results)]
        extraction = self.extract(question, chunks)
        texts = {chunk.id: chunk.text for chunk in chunks}
        spans: dict[str, list[str]] = {chunk.text: [] for chunk in chunks}
        for span in extraction.spans:
            spans[texts[span.chunk_id]].append(span.text)
        return spans

The two copies of VerbatimTransform (verbatim_core/transform.py:54, verbatim_rag/transform.py:48) become one adapter in verbatim_core.

docs.title: The warning
docs.text:
verbatim_core has a _deprecation.py. It defines the library's warning class and builds every message in one format:

"""Deprecation warnings for the public API of verbatim_core and verbatim_rag."""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

from typing_extensions import deprecated as _deprecated


class VerbatimDeprecationWarning(DeprecationWarning):
    """Emitted when code uses a part of the API that will be removed."""


def _message(name: str, since: str, removed_in: str, use: str) -> str:
    return f"{name} is deprecated since {since} and will be removed in {removed_in}. Use {use}."


def deprecated(name: str, *, since: str, removed_in: str, use: str):
    """Mark a class, function or method as deprecated."""
    return _deprecated(_message(name, since, removed_in, use), category=VerbatimDeprecationWarning)


def warn_deprecated_argument(
    name: str, *, since: str, removed_in: str, use: str, stacklevel: int = 3
) -> None:
    """Warn about a deprecated argument, from inside the function that takes it."""
    warnings.warn(
        _message(name, since, removed_in, use), VerbatimDeprecationWarning, stacklevel=stacklevel
    )
  • The library has its own subclass of DeprecationWarning, VerbatimDeprecationWarning, exported from the package root. A user can silence ours without silencing others, and our tests can turn ours into errors.
  • DeprecationWarning is the category for warnings aimed at developers. Python shows it when the call comes from __main__, which covers scripts and notebooks, and pytest shows it in every test run. It stays hidden when the call comes from inside another installed package, whose users couldn't fix it. Python's default filter shows it once per call site, so a loop doesn't repeat it.
  • typing_extensions.deprecated (PEP 702) warns at runtime, makes type checkers and IDEs mark every use, and keeps the message in __deprecated__ for the API docs. It needs typing_extensions 4.5 or later. The package arrives through pydantic and openai already, and the library lists it as a direct dependency.
  • Warnings fire when the old name is used: constructed, called, or passed as an argument. Importing a module that defines a deprecated class never warns. A module that moved warns on attribute access through a module-level __getattr__. verbatim_rag/transform.py becomes such a module, re-exporting the names from verbatim_core.
  • The decorator can't mark an argument. A deprecated argument defaults to a sentinel, so the function can tell whether the caller passed it, and calls warn_deprecated_argument.

docs.title: Subclasses written against the old interface
docs.text:
Users subclass SpanExtractor today. The base class stays and keeps both sets of methods.

  • A subclass that implements only the old method keeps working. The base class's new method calls the old one, converts the result and warns once per class that the subclass should implement the new method. For such an extractor, offsets are recovered by searching the chunk, as today.
  • A subclass that implements only the new method gets the old method from the base class, through the adapter.
  • __init_subclass__ raises TypeError when a subclass implements neither, since the two default methods would call each other.
  • Our own extractors derive from the base class, so the base class itself is never marked with the decorator. The decorator would warn when our own subclasses are defined, at import time.

docs.title: Endpoints of the API server
docs.text: The FastAPI server in api/ keeps its routes and response shapes. A route replaced by a new one is marked with deprecated=True, which marks it in the OpenAPI document, and its responses carry Deprecation and Sunset headers (RFC 9745, RFC 8594). New routes return the core result types unchanged, so an API result has the same shape as a library result.

docs.title: Behaviour that changes through the old API
docs.text: The adapters keep today's shapes, but one behaviour changes, and it goes into the changelog: VerbatimRAG highlights the occurrence of a span the extractor chose, instead of every occurrence of the same text.

docs.title: New and replaced names
docs.text:
New in verbatim_core: the shared types, extract and aextract on every extractor, from_pretrained on the model extractors, Transformer, and _deprecation.py. New in verbatim_rag: VerbatimRAG(index, transformer=...), query_stream and SearchResult.to_chunk().

Old Replacement The adapter SpanExtractor.extract_spans, extract_spans_async extract, aextract groups the span texts by chunk text ModelSpanExtractor(model_path=...), SemanticHighlightExtractor(model_path=...) from_pretrained(model_id) calls from_pretrained LLMSpanExtractor() without llm_client LLMSpanExtractor(llm_client) builds LLMClient(model) as today VerbatimTransform, transform, transform_async Transformer, transform, atransform turns the context dicts into chunks and the Answer into a QueryResponse the module verbatim_rag.transform verbatim_core re-exports the core names verbatim_query, verbatim_query_async provider.retrieve followed by Transformer unchanged behaviour StreamingRAG, stream_query, stream_query_sync VerbatimRAG.query_stream yields today's event dicts VerbatimRAG(model=...), or without transformer VerbatimRAG(index, transformer=...) builds today's extractor and templates

Internal callers that move in the same pull request: verbatim_core/enhance.py:70 and verbatim_core/cli.py:54 (VerbatimTransform), verbatim_rag/verbatim_doc.py:135 (extract_spans_async), api/app.py:261 (the forked VerbatimTransform) and api/app.py:350 (StreamingRAG).

docs.title: The places that change
docs.text:
This table lists the places that change, in the same form as "Today's fallbacks" in the typed-errors document.

Where Today After the change verbatim_core/extractors.py:38 extract_spans returns dict[chunk_text, list[str]], so two chunks with the same text share one entry extract returns spans with chunk_id, offsets and score verbatim_core/extractors.py:222 the highlighter's character spans are reduced to their text offsets and score kept verbatim_core/extractors.py:131, :336 the constructors download and load the model from model_path from_pretrained, the constructor takes the loaded model verbatim_core/extractors.py:502 LLMClient(model) built when no client is passed client required, the old form warns verbatim_core/extractors.py:778, :838 the matchers locate each quote and return only its text they return the span with offsets verbatim_core/response_builder.py:122 highlights recovered with str.find, every occurrence of the text highlighted highlights from the span offsets verbatim_core/transform.py:70, verbatim_rag/transform.py:64 two copies of VerbatimTransform, each building LLMClient(), an extractor and templates when none are passed one Transformer, VerbatimTransform a deprecated adapter verbatim_rag/streaming.py:53, :68 streaming needs a VerbatimRAG with an index and sets rag.k per request Transformer.astream without an index, VerbatimRAG.query_stream(k=...) verbatim_rag/core.py:92 to :101 VerbatimRAG builds its client, extractor and templates from names takes a Transformer, the old form warns api/app.py:261 the transform route builds the forked VerbatimTransform() per request a Transformer built at startup

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: Tests check the behaviour, and review covers what tests don't see. No Ruff rule can tell whether code keeps state.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• standard-tests has one suite per interface (extractor, transformer). Every implementation runs it (see "Introduce multiple workspaces into the project structure"). The suites check that:
  • every span's text equals the slice at its offsets
  • the sync and async methods return equal results for the same input
  • a call with the model already loaded, run in an empty temporary directory set as working directory and HOME, leaves the directory empty
  • a second call with the same input returns the same result, also when a call with other input ran in between
  • usage has an entry with the model id and version.
  • Each package has a tests/test_deprecated.py. For each old entry point it checks the warning class and the message, and compares the result with today's output recorded on a few fixtures, so the adapter keeps today's shape.
  • pytest turns the library's own deprecation warnings into errors, so library code that calls a deprecated name fails the test suite. pytest.warns in test_deprecated.py records the warnings instead:
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
filterwarnings = [
    "error::verbatim_core.VerbatimDeprecationWarning",
]
  • Importing each package in a fresh interpreter emits none of the library's deprecation warnings.

docs.title: Review checklist
docs.text:
• Does an adapter do anything beyond converting arguments and results?
  • Does core code write a file, read an environment variable or keep anything on self between calls?
  • Does a constructor download, load or build a model or a client from a name?
  • Does a new result type carry usage and warnings?
  • Does every removed or renamed public name have an adapter, a warning with the library's class, and a changelog entry?

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
The steps are ordered so each one can ship on its own.

  1. Add the shared types and _deprecation.py to verbatim_core. Nothing changes behaviour yet.
  2. Add the standard-tests suites for the extractor and transformer interfaces.
  3. Add extract on every extractor and from_pretrained, then Transformer with streaming, with the response builder working from offsets.
  4. Turn the old entry points into adapters, move the internal callers, and turn on the pytest filter.
  5. Rebuild VerbatimRAG on the core: query and query_stream.
  6. Add the new routes to the API server and deprecate the old ones.
  7. Release 0.3.0 with "Deprecated" and "Changed" sections in the changelog and a migration page in the documentation site.
  8. Remove the adapters in the release that the deprecation window names.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: # Question Decision 1 How long is the deprecation window? Recommendation: deprecate in 0.3.0, remove in 0.5.0, and not earlier than three months after 0.3.0. 2 What does score hold when a method produces no probability, as in LLM span extraction? Recommendation: 1.0, documented as "extracted without a score", so score is always a number. 3 After the window, does VerbatimRAG(index) still build a default LLM client, or is the client required? Recommendation: required, with the READMEs showing the explicit form from 0.3.0 on.

docs.title: Verbatim RAG: Stop Hallucinating, Start Quoting
docs.text:
Historical design article. Some APIs, model ids, benchmark counts, and categorical claims below predate the current package. Use the repository README and public roadmap for the supported guarantee boundary and current model configuration.

Chill, I Ground!

TL;DR: - Extract, Don't Freely Rewrite: select source text spans and keep the evidence inspectable - Wrap Existing RAG: Integrate with LangChain/LlamaIndex in 15 lines of code - CPU-Only Pipeline: No GPU, no API costs, works offline (SPLADE + ModernBERT) -> lightweight and efficient - Template Control: Static, dynamic, or question-specific response formatting - Smart Chunking: Structure-aware with raw/enhanced dual-chunk system - Reference implementation: - Full RAG framework for experimentation - Optional cloud compute or local storage - API and frontend prototypes in the source repository

Quick Links: - ⭐ GitHub - PyPI - Paper - ACL BioNLP 2025 - Models - Fine-tuned extractors

docs.title: Extract, Don't Generate
docs.text:
The fundamental issue with RAG systems is that LLMs generate text probabilistically. Even when provided with perfect context, the model samples from a probability distribution over tokens, which inevitably introduces approximations, paraphrasing, and factual drift.

This problem can compound in agentic RAG systems when a query triggers several generative steps. The practical risk depends on the models, prompts, task, and how failures correlate; it should be measured on the target workflow rather than inferred from a fixed per-call probability.

Verbatim RAG takes a different approach: Instead of asking the LLM to generate an answer based on retrieved documents, we constrain it to extract exact text spans that answer the question. These spans are then composed into a response without any generative rewriting.

Why this helps: Extraction asks which source spans answer the question rather than asking a model to freely rewrite the evidence. Built-in verified paths return source text, reducing the factual surface available for unsupported generation.

The result is inspectable evidence text. Source truth, retrieval completeness, selection relevance, and contextual framing still require evaluation.

docs.title: Quickstart: Source excerpts in 15 lines
docs.text:
Install the required dependencies: 

!pip install verbatim-rag

Then create a Verbatim RAG system:

from verbatim_rag import VerbatimRAG, VerbatimIndex
from verbatim_rag.vector_stores import LocalMilvusStore
from verbatim_rag.embedding_providers import SpladeProvider
from verbatim_rag.schema import DocumentSchema

# 1. Create index (storage layer) - works on CPU!
store = LocalMilvusStore("./demo.db", enable_sparse=True, enable_dense=False)
embedder = SpladeProvider("opensearch-project/opensearch-neural-sparse-encoding-doc-v2-distill", device="cpu")
index = VerbatimIndex(vector_store=store, sparse_provider=embedder)

# 2. Add a document
doc = DocumentSchema(
    content="""
# Methods
We used two approaches: zero-shot LLM extraction and a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier on 58k synthetic examples.

# Results
The system achieved 42.01% accuracy on ArchEHR-QA.
""",
    title="Research Paper"
)
index.add_documents([doc])

# 3. Create the RAG pipeline
rag = VerbatimRAG(index, model="gpt-4o-mini")

# 4. Get source excerpts
response = rag.query("What approaches were used?")
print(response.answer)
# [1] We used two approaches: zero-shot LLM extraction and a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier on 58k synthetic examples.

Note: Use dense embeddings (SentenceTransformers, OpenAI) or hybrid search by swapping the embedding provider. See docs for details.

docs.title: Already Have a RAG System? Wrap It in 15 Lines
docs.text:
A key integration pattern: wrap your existing LangChain/LlamaIndex retrieval with Verbatim's extraction layer. Your indexing pipeline stays unchanged, you're only adding the verbatim extraction step on top of your existing retrieval.

Install the required dependencies: 

!pip install langchain langchain-openai langchain-community openai faiss-cpu langchain-text-splitters

Then wrap your existing LangChain RAG system: 

from verbatim_rag.providers import RAGProvider
from verbatim_rag import verbatim_query

# Your existing LangChain setup
from langchain_community.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain_community.vectorstores import FAISS
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_core.documents import Document

from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional

# 1. Create sample documents
docs = [
    Document(
        page_content="""
# Methods
We used two approaches: zero-shot LLM extraction and a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier on 58k synthetic examples.

# Results
The system achieved 42.01% accuracy on ArchEHR-QA.
        """,
        metadata={"title": "Research Paper 1", "source": "paper1.pdf", "year": 2025},
    )
]

# 2. Index with LangChain (your existing setup)
text_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=50)
splits = text_splitter.split_documents(docs)
embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings()
vectorstore = FAISS.from_documents(splits, embeddings)
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 5})


# 3. Wrap your LangChain retriever
class LangChainRAGProvider(RAGProvider):
    def __init__(self, langchain_retriever):
        self.retriever = langchain_retriever

    def retrieve(
        self, question: str, k: int = 5, filter: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        # Use LangChain's retrieval
        docs = self.retriever.invoke(question)

        # Convert to Verbatim format
        context = []
        for doc in docs[:k]:
            context.append(
                {
                    "content": doc.page_content,
                    "title": doc.metadata.get("title", ""),
                    "source": doc.metadata.get("source", ""),
                    "metadata": doc.metadata,
                }
            )
        return context


# 4. Use Verbatim with your existing LangChain RAG
provider = LangChainRAGProvider(retriever)
response = verbatim_query(provider, "What methods were used?", k=5)

print(response.answer)
# Output: [1] We used two approaches: zero-shot LLM extraction and a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier on 58k synthetic examples.

This approach preserves your existing retrieval system (embeddings, vector store, chunking strategy) while adding verbatim extraction. The only change is at the final answer generation step.

docs.title: Why This Matters
docs.text:
Even with perfect retrieval, the generation step introduces hallucinations. Consider this example:

Traditional RAG Verbatim RAG Question "How much synthetic data?" "How much synthetic data?" Retrieved "We created 60k examples" "We created 60k examples" Generated "Around 58,000 examples" "[1] We created 60k examples"

The LLM approximated "60k" to "58,000" during token generation—not because retrieval failed, but because the model is sampling from a learned distribution over approximate phrasings.

This happens because: 1. Token-level generation doesn't preserve exact numerals from context 2. Token prediction objective learns probability distributions over paraphrases, not verbatim copying mechanisms 3. Autoregressive sampling can drift from source text even with high context attention

Traditional RAG systems try to mitigate this through better prompting, retrieval, or reranking. But these don't address the root cause: the model is generating new tokens rather than selecting existing ones.

# Traditional RAG: Model generates tokens (probabilistic)
answer = "They generated approximately 58,000 synthetic training samples"

# Verbatim RAG: Model selects spans (deterministic given the extraction)
answer = "[1] We created 60k examples."

docs.title: Architecture: Two Independent Layers
docs.text: Verbatim RAG decouples retrieval from extraction through a clean interface boundary:

docs.title: Layer 1: VerbatimIndex (Storage)
docs.text: Handles document ingestion, chunking, embedding, and retrieval: - Input: Raw documents (PDFs, text, markdown) - Output: Top-k relevant chunks for a query - Components: Pluggable chunkers (markdown-aware, Chonkie), embedders (sparse/dense), vector stores (local/cloud Milvus)

docs.title: Layer 2: Verbatim Core (Extraction)
docs.text: Consumes retrieved chunks and produces verbatim answers: - Input: Query + retrieved chunks - Output: Source excerpts, with framing determined by the selected template mode - Components: Span extractors (LLM or fine-tuned models), template managers, verification

docs.title: The Interface
docs.text:
# Layer 1: Retrieval
chunks = index.query(question, k=5)  # Returns List[SearchResult]

# Layer 2: Extraction
spans = extractor.extract_spans(question, chunks)  # Returns Dict[str, List[str]]
answer = template_manager.compose(spans)  # Returns formatted response

This separation means you can: - Swap Layer 1 for your existing retrieval (LangChain, custom) - Use just Layer 2 to harden an existing RAG system - Replace components independently (e.g., switch from LLM to ModernBERT extractor without touching retrieval)

docs.title: Index Real Research Papers
docs.text:
from verbatim_rag.schema import DocumentSchema

# Add multiple papers with metadata
papers = [
    DocumentSchema.from_url(
        url="https://aclanthology.org/L16-1417.pdf",
        title="Building Concept Graphs from Monolingual Dictionary Entries",
        doc_type="academic_paper",
        authors=["Gabor Recski"],
        conference="LREC",
        year=2016,
    ),
    DocumentSchema.from_url(
        url="https://aclanthology.org/2025.bionlp-share.8.pdf",
        title="KR Labs at ArchEHR-QA 2025: A Verbatim Approach for Evidence-Based Question Answering",
        doc_type="academic_paper",
        authors=["Adam Kovacs", "Paul Schmitt", "Gabor Recski"],
        conference="BioNLP",
        year=2025,
    ),
]

index.add_documents(papers)

Search with metadata filtering:

# Find papers from BioNLP
results = index.query(
    filter='metadata["conference"] == "BioNLP"',
    k=10
)

for result in results:
    print(f"{result.metadata['title']} ({result.metadata['year']})")
    print(f"Score: {result.score:.3f}")

For production, use cloud storage:

from verbatim_rag.vector_stores import CloudMilvusStore

store = CloudMilvusStore(
    uri="https://your-milvus-instance.com",
    token="your-token",
    collection_name="production"
)

docs.title: CPU-capable pipeline without generative LLM API calls
docs.text:
After model weights are available, retrieval and extraction can run on CPU without a generative LLM API call when static rendering is selected:

from verbatim_rag.extractors import ModelSpanExtractor
from verbatim_rag.embedding_providers import SpladeProvider

# SPLADE for embeddings (sparse representations are CPU-efficient)
embedder = SpladeProvider("opensearch-project/opensearch-neural-sparse-encoding-doc-v2-distill", device="cpu")

# ModernBERT for extraction (fine-tuned on span classification)
extractor = ModelSpanExtractor(
    model_path="KRLabsOrg/verbatim-rag-modern-bert-v2",
    device="cpu"
)

# Complete CPU-only RAG
rag = VerbatimRAG(index, extractor=extractor, template_mode="static")

Tradeoffs: The fine-tuned extractor has lower recall than LLM-based extractors on complex queries, but is deterministic, free, and works offline.

docs.title: Template Management
docs.text: Template management controls how extracted spans are composed into final responses. Three modes are available:

docs.title: 1. Static Mode - Fixed Format
docs.text:
Use when response formatting must be identical across all queries:

template = """
Based on our research documents:
[RELEVANT_SENTENCES]

Need more information? Contact support@yourcompany.com
"""

rag.template_manager.use_static_mode(template)

response = rag.query("What methods were used?")
# Output:
# Based on our research documents:
# [1] We used zero-shot LLM extraction and fine-tuned ModernBERT.
#
# Need more information? Contact support@yourcompany.com

The [RELEVANT_SENTENCES] placeholder is automatically replaced with numbered citations.

Use cases: Compliance-required formatting, API responses with fixed schemas, systems where output format must be predictable.

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Mode - Adaptive Formatting (Default)
docs.text:
The LLM generates a context-appropriate template for each query:

rag.template_manager.use_contextual_mode()  # Default

response = rag.query("Who are the authors?")
# Gets: "The authors are: [1] ..."

response = rag.query("What were the results?")
# Gets: "The system achieved: [1] ..."

Use cases: Conversational interfaces, chatbots, systems where natural language flow matters more than format consistency.

docs.title: 3. Question-Specific Mode - Template Matching
docs.text:
Sometimes you want different response formats for different question types, without the randomness. Define templates paired with example questions—the system automatically selects the best-fitting template using semantic similarity:

templates = [
    {
        "template": "**Methodology:**\n\n[RELEVANT_SENTENCES]\n\n*Methods extracted from source*",
        "examples": [
            "What methods were used?",
            "How was this done?",
            "Describe the methodology"
        ]
    },
    {
        "template": "**Key Findings:**\n\n[RELEVANT_SENTENCES]\n\n*Results from source*",
        "examples": [
            "What were the results?",
            "What did they find?",
            "What are the key findings?"
        ]
    }
]

rag.template_manager.use_question_specific_mode(templates)

# Questions automatically matched to appropriate templates
response = rag.query("How did they approach this?")
# Uses Methodology template

response = rag.query("What were the main findings?")
# Uses Key Findings template

The system embeds all example questions once and matches incoming queries using cosine similarity—no LLM call needed.

docs.title: Technical Tradeoffs
docs.text:
When to use Verbatim RAG:

Verbatim RAG trades generation flexibility for factual precision. Use it when: - Exactness matters: Medical dosages, legal citations, financial figures must be character-perfect - Auditability required: Every claim needs to trace back to source text - Liability concerns: Approximate or paraphrased answers create legal/compliance risk - Existing RAG needs a smaller generative surface: You want inspectable source excerpts alongside your existing retrieval

When traditional RAG may be preferable:

  • Synthesis across sources: Answering requires combining information from multiple passages in ways that don't exist verbatim in any single source
  • Natural language fluency: Responses need to be conversational and flowing, not citation-heavy
  • Abstract/analytical queries: Questions like "What are the main themes?" require interpretation, not extraction

Hybrid approach: Use Verbatim RAG for factual queries and traditional RAG for analytical/synthesis queries, routing based on query type.

docs.title: A span points at one occurrence of its text
docs.text: When a quote occurs more than once in a chunk, the extractor locates one occurrence: the first exact one, else the best fuzzy match, the earliest on a tie. Identical spans collapse into one, and the response builder keeps the first of any overlapping highlights. Until 0.3.0 the response builder searched for each span's text afterwards and highlighted every occurrence. That made the number of citations depend on how often a phrase repeats, not on what the extractor chose, and it can't be expressed with offsets.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Repeated text now gets one highlight and one citation instead of one per occurrence. The 0.3.0 changelog says so under "Changed".

docs.title: Chunk ids are the index's row ids
docs.text: SearchResult.to_chunk() gives a chunk the id of its vector row (ProcessedChunk.id, a random UUID), so spans and citations can point at a chunk by id. The id is stable while the document stays indexed, and changes when the document is re-indexed.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text: • A deterministic "{document_id}:{chunk_number}", which survives re-indexing. Rejected: after a chunking change the same id silently points at different text, and a citation that resolves to the wrong text is worse than one that no longer resolves.

docs.title: query_stream yields typed events and ends with the query response
docs.text: VerbatimRAG.query_stream yields typed events: documents with the retrieved chunks, spans with the extracted spans, and a final event that carries the same QueryResponse that query returns for the same input, so tests can compare the two. Failures raise typed exceptions instead of arriving as an error event, and there is no progress event.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The deprecated StreamingRAG adapter rebuilds today's dict stream (documents, progress, highlights, answer, error) from the typed events, the exceptions and its own timing. The API server's streaming route keeps that dict stream until a new route replaces it.

docs.title: Structured template mode stays outside the stateless core
docs.text: In structured mode (template_mode="structured"), VerbatimRAG extracts by itself: it calls the LLM client's structured extraction directly instead of a SpanExtractor. It stays that way through the stateless-core rollout, as a deliberate exception to "the stateful classes only retrieve, store and call the core", because issue #74 redesigns structured answers (a JSON answer with a span per field) and would replace whatever the rollout built.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Transformer raises when asked for structured mode.
  • VerbatimRAG keeps an llm_client argument for structured mode alone, and structured mode without one raises.
  • use_structured_mode and the structured template's setup keep working without warnings. The whole structured API is deprecated in one step when #74 provides the replacement.
  • fill_async and set_rag_system, which let the templates call back into VerbatimRAG, are deprecated now in favour of VerbatimRAG.query_async.

docs.title: Random template mode chooses by question, not at random
docs.text: Random template mode picks its template from a hash of the question that is the same in every process (so not Python's hash()), optionally combined with a seed from TransformConfig. The stateless core promises the same result for the same input, and a template drawn with random.choice on every call broke that. The mode's purpose, variety across questions, doesn't need randomness per call. The same question now always gets the same template.

docs.title: A failed LLM call fails the whole extraction
docs.text: When an LLM call fails during span extraction, extract raises a typed error instead of returning no spans for the chunks that call covered. Until 0.3.0 the extractor logged the error and returned empty results, so a caller couldn't tell "nothing relevant in this chunk" from "this chunk was never examined", and an answer built from the remaining chunks looked complete. Retrying is the job of the LLM-call layer, not the extractor.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The fallback from one batch call to one call per chunk survives only in the deprecated extract_spans path.

docs.title: verbatim_core.transformer.Transformer
docs.text:
Turn a question and chunks into a cited answer, built from spans of the chunks.

The first spans fill the template of the answer, and every span gets one citation that points at it by chunk id and offsets. One transformer can serve concurrent calls: the settings of a call come in its config, and nothing is set on the transformer between calls.

Source code in packages/core/verbatim_core/transformer.py 
class Transformer:
    """Turn a question and chunks into a cited answer, built from spans of the chunks.

    The first spans fill the template of the answer, and every span gets one citation that points
    at it by chunk id and offsets. One transformer can serve concurrent calls: the settings of a
    call come in its config, and nothing is set on the transformer between calls.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        extractor: SpanExtractor[Any],
        templates: TemplateManager,
        *,
        config: TransformConfig | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Build a transformer from an extractor and the templates of the answers.

        :param extractor: Extracts the spans of the chunks
        :param templates: The templates the answers are written with
        :param config: The settings of a call, unless the call passes its own. Without it, the
            templates' settings are the default.
        :raises ConfigurationError: If the config is not a TransformConfig, or asks for structured
            template mode
        """
        self.extractor = extractor
        self.templates = templates
        self._config = None if config is None else _default_config(config, TransformConfig)
        # Templates in structured mode raise at the call: VerbatimRAG answers structured
        # questions itself with the same templates (ADR 0004).
        if self._config is not None and self._config.template_mode == "structured":
            raise ConfigurationError(_STRUCTURED_MODE_UNSUPPORTED, code="invalid_value")
        if templates.strategy(self.config.template_mode) is None:
            warn_contextual_without_client()

    @property
    def config(self) -> TransformConfig:
        """The settings of a call that passes none: the config given, else the templates'."""
        return self._config if self._config is not None else self.templates.config

    def transform(self, question: str, chunks: Sequence[Chunk], *, config: TransformConfig | None = None) -> Answer:
        """Write a cited answer to the question from the chunks.

        :param question: The question
        :param chunks: Chunks with unique ids
        :param config: Replaces the transformer's default config for this call
        :return: The answer, with its citations, spans, usage and warnings
        :raises InvalidInputError: If two chunks share an id, or the config is of the wrong type
            or asks for structured template mode
        :raises UpstreamError: If a service the extractor calls fails
        :raises ConfigurationError: If a service rejects its key, model or quota
        """
        config, strategy = self._call_settings(config)
        *_, answer_event = self._events(question, chunks, config, strategy)
        # The last event is always the answer.
        return cast("AnswerEvent", answer_event).answer

    async def atransform(
        self, question: str, chunks: Sequence[Chunk], *, config: TransformConfig | None = None
    ) -> Answer:
        """Async version of `transform`."""
        config, strategy = self._call_settings(config)
        events = [event async for event in self._aevents(question, chunks, config, strategy)]
        return cast("AnswerEvent", events[-1]).answer

    def stream(
        self, question: str, chunks: Sequence[Chunk], *, config: TransformConfig | None = None
    ) -> Iterator[TransformEvent]:
        """Write the answer of `transform` as events: the spans, then the answer.

        :raises InvalidInputError: When called, if the config is of the wrong type or asks for
            structured template mode. The other errors of `transform` come from the iteration.
        """
        config, strategy = self._call_settings(config)
        return self._events(question, chunks, config, strategy)

    def astream(
        self, question: str, chunks: Sequence[Chunk], *, config: TransformConfig | None = None
    ) -> AsyncIterator[TransformEvent]:
        """Async version of `stream`."""
        config, strategy = self._call_settings(config)
        return self._aevents(question, chunks, config, strategy)

    def _call_settings(self, config: TransformConfig | None) -> tuple[TransformConfig, TemplateStrategy]:
        """Return the config and the template strategy of one call."""
        call_config = _call_config(config, self.config, TransformConfig)
        if call_config.template_mode == "structured":
            if config is None:
                # The templates' settings, switched to structured mode after construction
                raise ConfigurationError(_STRUCTURED_MODE_UNSUPPORTED, code="invalid_value")
            raise InvalidInputError(_STRUCTURED_MODE_UNSUPPORTED, code="invalid_value", param="config.template_mode")

        strategy = self.templates.strategy(call_config.template_mode)
        if strategy is None:
            # Only contextual mode needs a client. Until the deprecation window ends, it falls
            # back to static templates.
            warn_contextual_without_client()
            # Static mode needs no client, so it always has a strategy.
            strategy = cast("TemplateStrategy", self.templates.strategy("static"))
        return call_config, strategy

    def _events(
        self,
        question: str,
        chunks: Sequence[Chunk],
        config: TransformConfig,
        strategy: TemplateStrategy,
    ) -> Iterator[TransformEvent]:
        logger.debug("Transforming %d chunks in %s mode", len(chunks), config.template_mode)
        extraction = self.extractor.extract(question, chunks)
        yield SpansEvent(spans=extraction.spans)
        display, references = _split(extraction.spans, config)
        template = strategy.generate_result(question, _texts(display + references), len(references), seed=config.seed)
        yield AnswerEvent(answer=_answer(extraction, template, display, references, _fill(strategy, config)))

    async def _aevents(
        self,
        question: str,
        chunks: Sequence[Chunk],
        config: TransformConfig,
        strategy: TemplateStrategy,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[TransformEvent]:
        logger.debug("Transforming %d chunks in %s mode", len(chunks), config.template_mode)
        extraction = await self.extractor.aextract(question, chunks)
        yield SpansEvent(spans=extraction.spans)
        display, references = _split(extraction.spans, config)
        template = await strategy.generate_result_async(
            question, _texts(display + references), len(references), seed=config.seed
        )
        yield AnswerEvent(answer=_answer(extraction, template, display, references, _fill(strategy, config)))

class TransformConfig(BaseModel):
    """Settings of a `Transformer` call."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid", hide_input_in_errors=True)

    # The first spans are shown in the answer, the rest are cited for reference only.
    max_display_spans: NonNegativeInt = 5
    # The Transformer rejects "structured": structured answers stay in VerbatimRAG (ADR 0004).
    template_mode: Literal["static", "contextual", "random", "question_specific", "structured"] = "static"
    citation_mode: Literal["inline", "hidden"] = "inline"  # citation markers in the text, or none
    citation_format: str = "[{number}]"  # the marker, with {number} and {span_id}
    seed: int | None = None  # random template mode chooses by the question and this seed

    @field_validator("citation_format")
    @classmethod
    def validate_citation_format(cls, citation_format: str) -> str:
        try:
            citation_format.format(number=1, span_id="1")
        except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError) as e:
            msg = "citation_format may use only {number} and {span_id}"
            raise ValueError(msg) from e
        return citation_format
